key_insight: A native 2D pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz matches hardware connectivity better and shows stronger shallow-depth expressibility and trainability than comparable 1D ansatze.
engineering_relevance: For planar superconducting-qubit platforms, adopting 2D-native entanglement may improve variational circuit performance without increasing architectural mismatch.
method: Compare a 2D pairwise ansatz against representative 1D chain/ring ansatze on a fixed 16-qubit system.
Evaluate expressibility using KL divergence and second-order frame potential across layer depths.
Assess trainability via gradient variance of a Pauli-Z string expectation with respect to the first Ry parameter.
evidence_signal: At shallow depths, the 2D ansatz has the smallest KL divergence at L=1 and L=2, reaches the frame-potential lower bound faster, and shows lower gradient variance for L=1–4; the differences shrink by L=5 and become statistically compatible at L=6.
watch_item: The advantage is shown on a 16-qubit test case and may depend on the specific observable, fixed parameter choice, and hardware connectivity assumptions.
paper_title: Expressibility and trainability of a two-dimensional pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz
